<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a8b44d407028cde9886b193f1add17a53437b03c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

Seat ACCEPT · epic PM `session_01Y5583bs2RDd53MH6kM1ca3` (`os-steve`) · 2026-10-20T14:23Z. PR #24911 at `e6861886060f0876a2e79bf7e0765ff6673b7bc5` (#24884 Part 2, os-dev-report 6292657948 on #24884). **ACCEPT.**

## Seat check

- **Shape.**
  - 7 paths, +2229/−15 = 2,244 lines, all under `packages/qa/dogfood/test/` plus `scripts/gen-upgrade-harness-fixture.mjs`. The dump and manifest are 2,061 of those lines.
  - `check-governed-merges --branch`: NOT governed, under 3,000 lines. Not Tier H.
  - The body says `Clause-②: no`; there is no published schema and no governed path. No contract face is touched, so no second-agent review is owed (contract-review.md, "none of the four faces ⇒ CI plus the seat's own read"). This is that read.
- **Premises, measured in the committed fixture.**
  - The birth marker is `{shapeGeneration: 1, platformVersion: "18.0.0"}`.
  - The dump holds 15 `COALESCE` unique indexes.
  - A scan for credential-shaped strings in `fixture-18.0.0/database.sql` (token prefixes, access-key ids, PEM headers) found none.
- **Code read.**
  - The new leg reads the GA fixture into a temp SQLite file. It asserts four things:
    - the marker, and that every reshaped table holds rows;
    - `os migrate plan --json` over it lists no `destructive` change;
    - HEAD boots it with no refusal and no error, both fixture people sign in, and the edited task is served;
    - after stop, every census row is still there with its key columns.
  - `takeCensus` leaves `organization_id` out only on the two `dropsOrganization` tables, and only when the column is absent. Any other missing key column is still a failure.
  - The populator keeps the pre-release path (`PATCH` the seeded mirror row) and adds the 18.0.0 path (`POST /security/_activation/webhook/:name`, then an organization webhook authored under a new name).
  - The generator now skips only the `fixture-*` directories, so `fixture-manifest.ts` comes from HEAD.
  - `fixture-18.0/` is unchanged.
- **Gate check-runs on the head.**
  - `18.x upgrade harness (opt-in)`: success, job 118671826332. Its log shows `upgrade-18x-harness.dogfood.test.ts` 12/12, the four new tests among them.
  - Required checks: TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core, Lint & Repo Gates and Governed Surface Queue Guard all succeeded. All 42 latest check-runs are success or skipped.
- **Accepted deviation.** None.
- **Out of scope, and where it goes.** 7b-0 (tenant column NOT NULL at create) and 7b-1+7b-2 (#24893, plain index form) change this baseline. Each must keep this leg green on its own head. Both devs have been told, and both PRs carry `needs:upgrade-harness`.
- **Landing.** This is an ordinary queue landing (not governed, not Tier H): the seat flips it ready and enables auto-merge. The PR merges clean with `main` after 7z (`0091d845e2`).
